steps_walked.title: Country codes shown as three letters (ISO alpha-3), with the full country name in the hover bubble
prerequisites: BROWSER: a Chromium-based browser (Chrome, Chromium, Edge or Brave). The gate closes on 'a Chromium click-through record', and the country names in the hovers come from the browser's own name data, so another browser may word a few of them differently.

YOUR REAL INSTALL: the normal encrypted app, unlocked, at http://127.0.0.1:8000, with your real corpus. Steps L10 and L11 need data that only an install that has collected online holds: market series, and World Bank country figures. L11 explains the one online, consented load if the figures are missing.

A THROWAWAY INSTALL for the steps that change data or need known data (L1, L12; optional for L7 and L8). From the app folder (the one containing install.sh), with a NEW EMPTY folder that is never your real data folder: (1) seed it BEFORE starting any server: OO_DATA_DIR=$HOME/oo-throwaway-alpha3 OO_DB_PLAINTEXT=1 .venv/bin/python scripts/ui_clickthrough_seed.py --mini ; (2) start it on a different port so it cannot collide with the real app: OO_DATA_DIR=$HOME/oo-throwaway-alpha3 OO_DB_PLAINTEXT=1 .venv/bin/python -m uvicorn src.api.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8010 ; (3) open http://127.0.0.1:8010. Do NOT add the OO_NO_SCHEDULER=1 the sandbox walk used: that flag skips turning airplane mode on at startup. Accept or skip any first-launch screens (language, privacy policy, wizard) and answer 'Not now' to anything that offers to go online. To undo: Ctrl-C the server, then delete $HOME/oo-throwaway-alpha3.

AIRPLANE MODE ON in both instances: the plane icon in the top bar is FILLED. If it is hollow on your real install, click it once to engage airplane mode. That also stops collection. If the 'Go online?' popup appears in any step other than L11, press 'Stay offline'.
The interface starts in English: the top-bar language button shows a flag and 'EN'.

WHERE SUBTABS ARE: section tabs such as Countries · Compare · Groups · Map · Law · Statistics, the Agenda views (Month … List), the Library views, the World map lenses and the Settings sections appear in a row just under the top bar, not inside the page.
A text editor or spreadsheet program for opening one downloaded CSV file (L4).

steps.where: Throwaway (port 8010), or your real install if its law table already has rows: Governments (sidebar) → Law (subtab) → the 'Legal changes' panel and the 'Tracked laws' table below it (#law-changes, #law-docs)
steps.do: Throwaway only: press 'Re-seed catalog' once. It is local and makes no network request; it only adds catalogue rows. Wait for the message 'Seeded … sources, … laws.' Then scroll to 'Tracked laws' and hover these codes in the 'Jurisdiction' column: GBR, DEU, EUU, INT. On your real install, skip Re-seed. Do NOT press 'Track changes now' or 'Add & track now', because both fetch from the internet. Do not click the 'stop' / 'resume' links either, because they change what is tracked.
steps.expect: Every Jurisdiction cell is exactly three UPPERCASE letters, from this set: GBR, DEU, EUU, INT, CAN, USA, FRA. Lowercase 'uk', 'eu', 'int' or 'de' never appear. Each code has a dotted underline, and hovering it opens the app's styled hover bubble with the full name: GBR → 'United Kingdom' (the catalogue stores this one as 'uk'), DEU → 'Germany', EUU → 'European Union — not an ISO code', INT → 'International — not an ISO code'. The real countries (GBR, DEU, FRA, CAN, USA) carry NO 'not an ISO code' tail. 'Legal changes' will be empty in the throwaway because nothing has been tracked there. On your real install, the bold code at the start of each change follows the same rule.

verdicts.title: 28 real ISO 3166-1 codes, Vatican City among them, are missing from the alpha-3 table and show as two-letter codes that hover 'not a recognised country code'
verdicts.reason: Reproduced on my own encrypted instance on port 8824 (default seed plus the walker's seed_extra.py). In Settings > Advanced > Sources the Country filter lists 'Anguilla (ai) ·1', 'Cook Islands (ck) ·1' and 'Vatican City (va) ·2'. With Vatican City ticked, the table cell reads 'va' and its title and #oo-tip read 'not a recognised country code', while the filter right beside it names the same code 'Vatican City'. In the Calendar directory, AI, AX, BQ, BV and IO all hover 'not a recognised country code'. Library > World coverage shows rows va/ai/ck and 31 lowercase 'Not covered' pills (aq, ax, bl … yt), all with the same hover. The app's /api/catalog/export.csv rows for va and ck end with an empty country_iso3. The walker undercounted: the gap is 34 codes, not 28. No ruling or brief exempts these codes. Gate row L says 'every code the user sees is alpha-3 … the full country name … in the hover'. Severity P2: the hover makes a false statement about valid ISO codes, and the export drops iso3 for real rows.
verdicts.root_cause: src/catalog/countries.py:622-640 _ISO3_TO_2_TEXT, and its verbatim mirror at src/static/app-core.js:64-81, list only World Bank economies plus a few territories. 34 members of ISO_3166_1_ALPHA2 have no pair: ai aq ax bl bq bv cc ck cx eh fk gf gg gp gs hm io je mf mq ms nf nu pm pn re sh sj tf tk um va wf yt. For these, ooCountryCode (app-core.js:141-154) falls through to the raw value, ooCountryKind returns 'unresolved', and ooCountryTitle returns 'not a recognised country code'. On the server, country_display_code and country_payload_iso3 fall back the same way, so country_iso3 is empty.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Add the 34 pairs to BOTH texts in the same order: ala:ax aia:ai ata:aq atf:tf blm:bl bes:bq bvt:bv cck:cc cok:ck cxr:cx esh:eh flk:fk guf:gf ggy:gg glp:gp sgs:gs hmd:hm iot:io jey:je maf:mf mtq:mq msr:ms nfk:nf niu:nu spm:pm pcn:pn reu:re shn:sh sjm:sj tkl:tk umi:um vat:va wlf:wf myt:yt. That keeps the test_country_display parity test green. Also add one assertion that every ISO_3166_1_ALPHA2 member has an alpha-3 pair; it would have caught this gap.

verdicts.title: The Manage sources filter row collapses at 375 px and the Country filter cannot be opened
verdicts.reason: Reproduced at 375x800 in en. Page horizontal scroll is 0, but the filter wrappers resolve to 13 px each: Search box 25 px wide; the Language, Country, Type and Tags controls start at x=71/95/118/142, each 90 px wide, so they overlap. The labels print on top of each other, and the Enabled select covers the rest (screenshot R4). A Playwright click on #src-msel-country > summary times out because it is intercepted, and a scan along its midline finds no point where the summary itself is the hit target. So the Language, Country and Type filters cannot be used at phone width. This is not an alpha-3 issue, but it is a real defect.
verdicts.root_cause: The phone-width override at src/static/app.css:1720 (`.row > div { min-width:0 }`) combines with `.row > div { flex:1 }` (app.css:440, flex-basis 0). Every wrapper therefore fits on one line and flex-wrap never wraps. `.msel > summary { min-width:90px }` (app.css:759-761) then overflows each ~13 px wrapper, and later siblings paint over it.
verdicts.suggested_fix: In the phone media block, give these wrappers a wrapping basis, for example `.row > div:has(> details.msel) { flex:1 1 130px; }`, or `.row > div { flex-basis:140px; }` while keeping min-width:0. The filters then wrap onto their own lines, and the page still never widens.
